infoYearT1.evidence_source: [/page/2/Text/5] The current study extends prior research on the integrative adjustment model. Whereas Lent et al. (2013) tested the model crosssectionally and Navarro et al. (2014) examined the model longitudinally at two time points, the present study tested relations among the variables at three points in time. In particular, we followed up the participants in the Lent et al. study who had originally completed the SCCT measures at the end of their first semester.

Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/2/Text/7] In particular, as hypothesized by Lent, Taveira, Sheu, and Singley (2009), we examined whether self-efficacy and social support might produce reciprocal paths to positive affect. We also examined the possibility of reciprocal paths between self-efficacy and social support and between self-efficacy and interest (Lent, Sheu, Gloster, & Wilkins, 2010). In addition, we explored possible bidirectional paths between interest and satisfaction (e.g., whether pursuit of one's interests promotes satisfaction with the academic environment, as suggested by Lent et al., 2013, and/or whether such satisfaction promotes interests).[/page/2/Text/8] Positive adjustment was defined in terms of satisfaction and intended choice persistence over time.
